## Overview

The Tidebound Brotherhood are the western barbarian tribe of Kythoria, their territory lying along the western coast and extending deep into the surrounding seas. Unlike the other tribes, their frontier is not defined by a single border — the sea is their frontier. They serve as the western frontier order. Their culture revolves around freedom, reputation, and the sea; they are not particularly interested in where someone came from, only in what they can do.

---

## Territory

The Tidebound Brotherhood's territory lies along the western coast of Kythoria and extends deep into the surrounding seas. Their settlements are built around ports, islands, fortified harbors, and coastal strongholds. The greatest of these settlements serves as the heart of the Brotherhood — a massive port where ships from across Kythoria can be found alongside vessels belonging to the Brotherhood itself. Its docks are crowded with sailors, merchants, hunters, mercenaries, and adventurers. Taverns stand beside shipyards, bounty boards stand beside markets, and warehouses stand beside training yards. It is a place where someone could arrive with nothing and leave with a ship, a crew, and a contract — or arrive as a wanted criminal and disappear into the crowd.

---

## Culture

Tidebound culture revolves around freedom, reputation, and the sea. They are not particularly interested in where someone came from — what matters is what they can do. A noble who cannot handle themselves on a ship is worth little to a Tidebound crew. A former criminal who can navigate a storm, track a monster, and keep their crew alive may earn enormous respect.

Their culture is therefore unusually diverse. Different crews may have completely different traditions, beliefs, and methods. There is no single way to be Tidebound. The Brotherhood's identity comes from belonging to something larger than oneself while retaining the freedom to live according to one's own code.

---

## Philosophy

The Tidebound believe that freedom is worth fighting for. They distrust institutions that demand absolute obedience: kings, governments, religious authorities, and even the other barbarian tribes. They have spent centuries dealing with people who attempt to control the sea and the people who live upon it. The Brotherhood's philosophy can essentially be summarized as: *"No chain holds those who know how to sail."*

However, their concept of freedom has always been morally complicated. To some, freedom means refusing tyranny. To others, it means doing whatever they want. This distinction has caused much of the Brotherhood's controversial history.

---

## The Brotherhood's Code

Unlike the other tribes, the Tidebound do not possess a rigid philosophical doctrine. Instead, individual crews traditionally follow their own codes. Nevertheless, several principles have become almost universally respected:

- A crew protects its own
- A debt must be repaid
- A contract must be honored
- No one owns the sea

These principles are not always followed perfectly, but breaking them can destroy someone's reputation within the Brotherhood — and reputation is one of the most valuable currencies a Tidebound member possesses.

---

## The Rite of Passage

The Tidebound do not have a single standardized rite shared by the entire Brotherhood. Instead, a recruit must earn the acceptance and respect of their crew. Traditionally, this means being entrusted with a task that tests their ability to survive without someone constantly protecting them. For some, it may be their first bounty; for others, an expedition into dangerous waters. The specific challenge does not matter — what matters is returning with a story worth telling.

---

## Attitude

Tidebound members tend to be independent, charismatic, adventurous, irreverent, unpredictable, opportunistic, fiercely loyal to their crews, suspicious of authority, and comfortable operating outside conventional morality. They are often more willing than the other tribes to take risks.

---

## Most Common Classes

- Rogue
- Artificer
- Ranger
- Fighter
- Barbarian
- Sorcerer

---

## Weapons & Equipment

Tidebound equipment is defined by practicality and adaptability. Their weapons commonly include cutlasses, longswords, rapiers, daggers, handaxes, pistols, bows, crossbows, harpoons, and improvised weapons. Armor is generally lighter than that of the Sunforged Legion — mobility is essential aboard ships. A Tidebound warrior must be able to fight on a deck, climb rigging, swim, board another vessel, and survive being thrown into the sea.

---

## Controversies

The Tidebound Brotherhood has never had a spotless history. Throughout the centuries, individual crews have been accused of raiding, piracy, smuggling, illegal salvage, black-market trade, contract killing, and operating outside the authority of kingdoms. The Brotherhood has occasionally fought against these practices internally, particularly when they threatened the organization's reputation or endangered innocent civilians — but it has never completely eliminated them.

This has created a complicated relationship between the Brotherhood and the governments of Kythoria. They are often considered criminals. Yet when a monster attacks a remote coastal settlement, those same governments may still turn to them for help.

---

## Relationship with Monsters

The Tidebound have a highly pragmatic relationship with monsters. They see monsters as threats, targets, and opportunities. A monster threatening a village is a bounty; a dangerous creature aboard a ship is a problem. The Brotherhood is willing to work with creatures that the other tribes would never tolerate. This has made them particularly effective in situations where conventional rules have failed.
